rules.title: The repository documents how it works
rules.description: Durable, repository-backed documentation describes the architecture, written for both a returning human and an agent with no conversation history.
rules.rationale: An agent cannot ask a colleague and will act on whatever the repository says.
rules.remediation: Run /codebase-docs, or reproduce its behaviour manually.
rules.$assuranceNote: Existence and substance are checked; accuracy is not.

rules.title: Documentation does not contradict the implementation
rules.description: A documented command, flag, path, or field that does not exist is a defect, not stale prose.
rules.rationale: An agent given a README describing a flag that does not exist will use the flag.
rules.remediation: Correct the document, or remove the wrong claim. Do not leave it with a caveat.
rules.$assuranceNote: Only documented PATHS are compared against the filesystem, and only those written as inline code spans; markdown links, fenced blocks and bare prose are not read. Behaviours, flags, and defaults are not checked. A path is resolved from the repository root, which is a convention the document is not obliged to follow: a token beginning with './' is relative to a working directory and is reported not-evaluated unless one is established, and a token whose containing directory is absent from the root is reported as unresolved rather than missing, because nothing corroborates the root as its base. Both still fail the rule; neither asserts the document is wrong.

rules.title: Diagrams are generated from canonical Mermaid source
rules.description: The .mmd source is canonical and retained; rendered SVG and embedded copies derive from it and are regenerated when it changes.
rules.rationale: A hand-edited render is a second definition of the architecture, and it is the one that drifts.
rules.remediation: Author the diagram in Mermaid, embed or render from it, and never hand-edit the output.
